summary: Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (circa 1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (circa 1955–1956), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia around 1942.

Byung-gon Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Rissho University (attested 2007). He serves as professor, dean, and research institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. C. Berg (1900–1990) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University, earning his doctorate under G. A. J. Hazeu and Nicolaas Johannes Krom, and served as Professor of Javanese at Leiden from 1929 to 1972.

C. Collin Davies (1896–1974) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned his B.A. at Aberystwyth University and Ph.D. at Peterhouse, later serving as Lecturer in Indian History at SOAS (1926–1936) and Reader at Oxford (1936–1963).

C. D. Sebastian works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, had postdoctoral mentorship from Paul Williams and Gavin D'Costa, and is attested in 2016 as Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay.

C. Kunhan Raja (1895–1963) worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as the first University Professor of Sanskrit at Madras (1927) and Honorary Director at the Adyar Library and Research Centre.

C. M. Naim (1936–2025) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1958 to 1961, and later served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago from circa 2001 to 2025.

C. M. Ridding (1862–1941) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Girton College and the University of Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and T. W. Rhys Davids. She worked at Girton and Cambridge University Library.
C. Peter Bankart is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a post at Wabash College (attested 2003) and served as a Visiting Researcher at Dartmouth College.

C. Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University (Ph.D. 2010). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania and has been a professor at Pennsylvania State University since 2010.

C. R. Krishnamacharlu (b. 1888) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College, and served at the Archaeological Survey of India circa 1911–1943.

C. S. Srinivasachariar (1890–1951) was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. Over his career, he served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. (1949–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (circa 1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and served as a professor at Hartwick College from circa 2001 to 2020.

Caixi Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti (1910–1983) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served at the Government Museum in Chennai, the Indian Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins (1933–2013) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard, where he served as Victor S Thomas Professor (1959–2003) before becoming Distinguished Professor in Residence at the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).

Calvin Thomas (1854–1919) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Leipzig, later teaching modern languages at Michigan (1879–1896) and Germanic languages and literatures at Columbia University (1896–1919).

Cameron Bailey is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under doctoral supervisor Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yudru Tsomu. He has held academic posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz works in religious studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and became a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University's Weatherhead East Asian Institute in 2025.
